severities.breaks the standard: the file contradicts a written rule of the standard
severities.note: listed for a person to confirm

rules.title: Names are lowercase kebab-case, slash between levels, no spaces
Fixed order: role, then variant, then state
Semantic tokens are named by purpose, never by a colour value
A state is always its own last segment
State groups are complete and siblings are written the same way
States come from one list: default, hover, active, focus, selected, disabled
One size scale xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl; no names taken from a pixel value
Size words come from the one scale: xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl
Primitives are named by value and are all used
Every semantic token aliases a primitive, written the same way as its siblings
Mode names are lowercase words; a one-mode collection calls its mode default
Collections are named for their category
Every semantic token has a one-line description
Every token has scopes that match its job, never all scopes
Every token has WEB code syntax, and it follows the naming rule
CSS prefixes follow the Tailwind v4 theme namespaces in the standard's table
Each surface changes only the separator, never the words
One job per token: tokens that promise different jobs do not share a value
Colour tokens whose light and dark values are equal
Type scale: readable sizes, no page zoom on fields, no duplicate roles, numeric weights
Compact density keeps the steps apart and never grows
Token categories that have not been started

findings.message: These names use xsmall, small, base, medium or large instead of xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl.
These radius names are taken from a pixel value (the height of the thing they round), which the standard forbids.
These semantic names are numbers (the pixel value times ten), not the xs to 2xl scale. The standard names radius/height/20 as the example; it does not say whether a spacing step counts.

findings.message: 225 of 225 primitives have no WEB code syntax. Rule 10 says every token has one; rule 5 says components never reach primitives. Decide whether primitives get CSS names.
15 tokens use the CSS prefix --font-size- where the standard's table promises --text-.
15 tokens use the CSS prefix --line-height- where the standard's table promises --leading-.
1 tokens use the CSS prefix --font-family- where the standard's table promises --font-.

61 tokens end in /default in Figma but their code syntax drops the word default. The standard says each surface changes only the separator, never the words; the file does otherwise. Decide which one is right.
